title: Refuse `git checkout -B` or `git switch -C` of any branch a worktree holds
why: Coordinator 14:34 CST: `git checkout -B <current branch>` in an agent worktree left a stale index twice.
note: A guard change, so a build lane (test-author, builder, reviewer). Done check: a red test on `git checkout -B <current branch>` in an agent worktree. Nov 7 22:47 CST: lane roadmap-push-refusal-says-fetch (#1777) hit it twice more: an agent's `git checkout -B` left old files in the worktree and index (a sibling holder; see below). Possible false alarm in the same incident: the shared-trees guard refused restoring stale staged files that match origin's blobs in an agent worktree; unchecked. Scope widened (coordinator, 03:16 CST Nov 8): one rule refusing `checkout -B` or `switch -C` of any branch a worktree holds. Folded in: checkout-b-held-branch (git 2.43 lets `checkout -B <b>` / `switch -C <b>` reset a branch ANOTHER worktree has checked out, leaving that worktree's index stale; seen 02:49 CST Nov 8 in lane idle-lane-steps-unknown). Lane moved: session_013NEJL1N3YkCMouc1pELXyu ended 02:48 CST with its work on archive/checkout-b-current-branch; lane idle-lane-steps-unknown (session_013NEJL1VtpMs3Aw5JLtyvVD) takes it. Round 2 of #1889 measured that a plain own-worktree `checkout -B lane-x other` is harmless on git 2.43.0, so #1889 narrows to sibling holders only (coordinator ruling, 04:50 CST Nov 8). The Nov 7 22:47 CST incident was a sibling holder, not the own worktree: three agent worktrees each ran `git checkout -B <lane branch> origin/<lane branch>` while an earlier agent's worktree still held the branch; a commit in one moved the shared ref, and the holder showed staged reverts. Reproduced on git 2.43.0 in a scratch repo (lane roadmap-push-refusal-says-fetch, 04:51 CST Nov 8). The narrowing fits. Sighting (lane revive-1042, 05:16 CST Nov 8): an agent's `git checkout -B <branch>` moved a branch another worktree had checked out, leaving that tree's files stale; a commit there would have undone the agent's work. The lane's proposed step worktree-branch-moved-under is folded here. Follow-up after #1889 (`Merge after: #1889`, lane idle-lane-steps-unknown, 05:40 CST Nov 8): an own-branch subfolder allow test, the guard.py docstring order, and the `--git-dir` note (Fix: none, Until 2026-11-21). Sighting (coordinator 11:48 CST Nov 8): in lane habit-is-not-a-guard (session_013NEJKyoXvBfn7q6bpofjYg), a builder brief said `git checkout -B <branch>` inside the agent's worktree; it moved the branch ref the lane's own worktree stands on, and the stale index read as uncommitted work. Nothing lost. Remedy idea: a detached checkout plus `push HEAD:<branch>`. Coordinator asked for a new step agent-worktree-moves-parent-branch; triage folded it here, since this step's title covers it. Lane to confirm scope. Related: step brief-destructive-git.
